purpose: Make callisto-graph's plan_version() the real producer of VersionPlan.platform_writes and VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates for Fixed groups containing GroupMember::PlatformManifest entries, so a napi-rs platform package's own manifest gets bumped in lockstep with its owning package and the owner's optionalDependencies pointer to that platform package tracks the same target version. This is delivered end-to-end for npm platform manifests; Cargo-format (maturin) platform manifests are handled by the same format-agnostic OpenContext/ManifestRole::Canonical machinery (AC-002, AC-002b) but are not yet reachable through real workspace discovery (walk.rs's platform-manifest detection is npm-only today -- see non_goals). Also close two confirmed-dormant correctness gaps in apply_version_plan's existing consumption of these two VersionPlan fields (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs), so that once plan_version starts emitting real data, that data is applied safely and its ecosystem's lockfile is refreshed/staged like any other bump.
scope: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs::plan_version (new producer logic for platform_writes and optional_dep_updates, driven by Fixed-group GroupMember::PlatformManifest members and their owner's PlannedBump); crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs (PlatformWrite gains a `from: Version` field); crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs::apply_version_plan (active_ecosystems derivation extended to platform_writes/optional_dep_updates manifest paths; platform_writes dispatch loop gains a current==from precondition check mirroring the existing bump loops). Confirmed via code inspection: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs::compose_pr_body calls plan_version directly and only ever constructs a VersionPlan by calling render_pr_body_from_plan on plan_version's own output (pr_body.rs lines 21-27) -- it has no independent VersionPlan-construction path of its own for real (non-test) use, so it automatically inherits this track's fix with zero additional producer code. crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs::plan_snapshot, by contrast, builds its own VersionPlan literal (lines 131-143) with synthetic snapshot_versions and never calls plan_version, so it is genuinely a separate, unaddressed producer -- covered under non_goals below, not silently assumed.
non_goals: commands/snapshot.rs::plan_snapshot populating its own platform_writes/optional_dep_updates. Confirmed by direct inspection (snapshot.rs lines 100-143): plan_snapshot constructs VersionPlan independently of plan_version, using synthetic per-run snapshot_versions instead of real cascade-computed bump targets. A snapshot build's platform-manifest version (if any) would need to be a synthetic snapshot version, not the owner's real PlannedBump.to -- which is a different derivation than this track builds. Deferred to a separate track.

commands/pr_body.rs needing any code change in this track. Confirmed by direct inspection (pr_body.rs lines 16-27): compose_pr_body's only production code path calls plan_version and then renders its output -- it has no independent VersionPlan construction outside of its own unit tests. Once plan_version is fixed, pr_body's preview output reflects real platform_writes/optional_dep_updates with zero additional code. This is stated as a confirmed fact, not an assumption -- there is no separate 'pr_body producer' to defer.

Building a new planning-logic path for optionalDependencies updates unrelated to platform packages. OptionalDepUpdate's only production source added by this track is: an owner package's canonical manifest declares an existing DependencyEntry with kind == DepKind::Optional whose name matches a sibling GroupMember::PlatformManifest's `name` field in the same Fixed group, and that group's owner package received a real bump this run. An ordinary cross-package optionalDependencies relationship with no platform-manifest member involved is out of scope and produces no OptionalDepUpdate under this track's logic.

Any change to the Manifest trait, ManifestFormat::from_path, or update_optional_dependencies's internal logic (crates/callisto-manifests/src/{npm,cargo,python}.rs). All three already implement update_optional_dependencies and iter_dependencies correctly; this track only adds a new call site in plan_version that reads iter_dependencies() to discover existing optionalDependencies entries and a new call site in apply_version_plan's precondition check -- it does not modify these trait methods or their per-ecosystem implementations.

Redesigning apply_version_plan's write-batching (classify_manifest_writes, the batched-write groups feeding the loop at apply.rs lines 140-179). The platform_writes and optional_dep_updates dispatch loops (apply.rs lines 244-262) remain the two separate, sequential loops they are today; this track adds a precondition check and lockfile-ecosystem awareness to them without folding them into the batched-write groups.

Validating that a GroupMember::PlatformManifest's declared `owner: PackageId` actually resolves to a package present in the workspace graph. Group-membership validity is enforced by the existing group-loading/validation pipeline (crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs, crate::napi::NapiTargetsIndex) before plan_version ever runs; this track assumes group config already passed that validation and does not re-validate it. NOTE: this assumption does not silently extend to Cargo-format platform manifests ever being classified as GroupMember::PlatformManifest by that pipeline in the first place -- for Ecosystem::Cargo specifically, that classification cannot occur today through real discovery at all (see the dedicated non_goals entry below on walk.rs's Ecosystem::Npm-only gate, and AC-002b).

Extending crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs's real-workspace discovery to classify Cargo-format (maturin-style) platform manifests as GroupMember::PlatformManifest. Confirmed by direct inspection (walk.rs:199): the only site that registers a manifest into IdentityIndex.platform -- the mechanism config/groups.rs::resolve() relies on to produce GroupMember::PlatformManifest instead of an ordinary GroupMember::Package -- is gated by `if *eco == Ecosystem::Npm`, with no equivalent branch for `Ecosystem::Cargo`. Independently confirmed empirically: a real Cargo.toml platform sibling with `version.workspace = true`, run through the actual `Workspace::load` -> `plan_version` pipeline, resolves as an ordinary `GroupMember::Package` (producing its own independent PlannedBump) rather than a `GroupMember::PlatformManifest`, leaving `plan.platform_writes` empty for it. This track's plan_version/apply_version_plan machinery (AC-001 through AC-013) is written generically against `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` and the format-agnostic OpenContext/ManifestRole::Canonical pattern (see AC-002, AC-002b), so it will work correctly for Cargo platform manifests once this discovery extension ships -- but building that walk.rs extension, and proving the full real-discovery-to-plan_version path for Cargo end-to-end, is deferred to a separate track.

Handling a platform manifest declared in group config whose file does not exist on disk, or whose content cannot be read as valid JSON/TOML for its ecosystem, as anything other than a hard error. This track does not add graceful-degradation, warning-and-skip, or partial-plan behavior for an unreadable platform manifest -- it surfaces the existing ManifestFormat::from_path / Manifest::current_version error unchanged (see AC-008).

Testing constraint, not a pass/fail acceptance criterion: all tests for AC-001 through AC-013 (and AC-007b, AC-012b) must invoke commands::version::plan_version or apply::apply_version_plan directly as their entry point; a test that only calls an internal helper function and bypasses one of these two public entry points does not satisfy its corresponding criterion.

api_surface.name: PlatformWrite
api_surface.signature: pub struct PlatformWrite { pub manifest: PathBuf, pub version: Version, pub from: Version }
api_surface.description: Adds a `from: Version` field (previously only `manifest` and `version` existed, crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs lines 45-49) capturing the platform manifest's on-disk version as observed by plan_version at plan time. Consumed by apply_version_plan's platform_writes dispatch loop as the expected-current-version precondition, mirroring PlannedBump.from's role in the sibling bump loops. This is a breaking change to any code constructing PlatformWrite directly (existing test fixtures in apply.rs and any future snapshot/pr_body producer) -- all call sites must supply `from`.

api_surface.name: commands::version::plan_version
api_surface.signature: pub fn plan_version<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver, I: SeverityInference>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, inference: &I, opts: &VersionOptions) -> Result<VersionPlan, GraphError>
api_surface.description: Signature unchanged. Behavior changes: the returned VersionPlan.platform_writes and VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates are now populated per AC-001 through AC-008 (including AC-002b and AC-007b) instead of being hardcoded to Vec::new() (previously at commands/version.rs lines 262-263). Can now return a new error path (AC-008) when a Fixed group's platform manifest cannot be opened or read.

api_surface.name: apply::apply_version_plan
api_surface.signature: pub fn apply_version_plan<R: CommandRunner>(root: &Path, plan: &VersionPlan, runner: &R, opts: &ApplyOptions, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<ApplyOutcome, GraphError>
api_surface.description: Signature unchanged. Behavior changes: (1) active_ecosystems (apply.rs lines 325-349) is now also derived from plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates manifest paths, affecting which lockfiles get staged (AC-009, AC-010, AC-011) -- note npm has no refresh subprocess in apply_version_plan at all, only Cargo and Pypi do, so this extension only ever adds npm STAGING, never a new refresh command; (2) the platform_writes dispatch loop (apply.rs lines 244-252) gains a current-version precondition check against PlatformWrite.from before writing, returning GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion on mismatch instead of overwriting unconditionally, except for the idempotent-retry case (AC-012, AC-012b, AC-013).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a Fixed group with an owner Package member whose PlannedBump computes from version X to version Y this run, and a sibling GroupMember::PlatformManifest member in the same group with path P and name N, running commands::version::plan_version on that workspace produces a VersionPlan whose platform_writes contains exactly one PlatformWrite entry with manifest == P and version == Y (Y is the owner's bump target, not an independently computed value).

In the AC-001 scenario, PlatformWrite.from equals the resolved current version of the platform manifest at path P on disk at plan time -- either the version string declared directly in P (the ordinary case), or, when P is a Cargo.toml declaring `version.workspace = true`, the version resolved from the workspace root's `[workspace.package] version` (see AC-002b for that specific case). plan_version reads P via ManifestFormat::from_path(P) to detect format, constructs ManifestDecl::new(P, ManifestRole::Canonical, format) -- ManifestRole::Canonical is used unconditionally regardless of the owning GroupMember::PlatformManifest's own `role` field, so that a Cargo/TOML-formatted platform manifest (e.g. a maturin platform crate) does not trip ManifestDecl::new's Platform-role-vs-CargoToml-format rejection (crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:104-106) -- then opens it via callisto_manifests::open(&decl, &ctx) and calls .current_version() on the resulting handle. The OpenContext `ctx` is derived by plan_version using the exact same pattern apply_version_plan already uses (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:118-130): cargo_workspace via WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(root.join("Cargo.toml")).inheritance(), and npm_workspace_kind via callisto_manifests::detect_npm_workspace_kind(root) -- both derived from the real workspace root, not passed as None. This mirrors the ManifestRole::Canonical construction already used by apply_version_plan's platform_writes and optional_dep_updates dispatch loops (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:247,257), so plan-time and apply-time reads of a given platform manifest use the same role and the same context derivation and cannot diverge.

Scoped to the OpenContext/workspace-inheritance resolution logic this track builds (AC-002), NOT to real-workspace discovery of a Cargo platform manifest -- as of this spec, crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:199 (the only site that registers a manifest into IdentityIndex.platform, which is what allows config/groups.rs::resolve() to classify a member as GroupMember::PlatformManifest) is gated by `if *eco == Ecosystem::Npm` with no Ecosystem::Cargo branch, so no Cargo.toml can become a GroupMember::PlatformManifest through the real, disk-discovered call path today (see non_goals for the deferred discovery-extension work). This criterion instead verifies the resolution logic directly: given a Fixed group whose owner Package member receives a real PlannedBump to version Y this run (the same owner-bump precondition AC-001 requires -- without a real bump, no PlatformWrite is produced for any member, per AC-006, and the criterion would be vacuously satisfiable), and which also contains a GroupMember::PlatformManifest member constructed directly in the test's group/workspace fixture (via Workspace::load followed by pushing the member into ws.config.groups.fixed, per lib.rs's documented test-construction pattern -- NOT produced by walk.rs discovery) whose `role` field is set to ManifestRole::Platform { .. } (mirroring exactly what walk.rs:213-216 stores for a real npm platform manifest -- this pins AC-002's 'ManifestRole::Canonical unconditionally, regardless of the member's own role field' clause to something falsifiable: an implementation that forwarded member.role into ManifestDecl::new instead of hardcoding ManifestRole::Canonical would return Err(ModelError) per crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:104-106 and fail this criterion) and whose path P points at a Cargo.toml with `version.workspace = true` (a maturin platform crate inheriting its version from the workspace root, per crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:47-52's inherited_version detection), and the workspace's root Cargo.toml declares a `[workspace.package] version` (e.g. "3.2.1", resolved via WorkspaceInheritance per crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:580-587), calling commands::version::plan_version(&ws, ..) on that workspace returns Ok(..) and the resulting VersionPlan.platform_writes contains EXACTLY ONE entry with manifest == P, `from` == the resolved workspace version ("3.2.1") -- not an Err(ManifestError::WorkspaceInherited) and not a missing/empty entry -- and `version` == Y (the owner's bump target). This confirms plan_version's OpenContext derivation correctly resolves Cargo workspace-inherited versions and honors the unconditional-Canonical-role rule for any manifest already classified as GroupMember::PlatformManifest, regardless of how that classification arose, and that the AC-002 machinery is format-agnostic. It does NOT confirm that plan_version works end-to-end starting from a real, disk-discovered Cargo platform manifest -- that requires the walk.rs discovery extension described in non_goals, which this track does not build.

Given the AC-001 scenario, and the owner package's own canonical manifest contains an existing dependency entry with kind == DepKind::Optional whose name exactly matches the platform member's name N (e.g. 'my-lib.linux-x64-gnu'), plan_version's VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates contains an OptionalDepUpdate entry whose manifest is the owner's canonical manifest path and whose updates contains the pair (N, Y).

Given the AC-001 scenario, but the owner package's canonical manifest has no dependency entry (of any kind) whose name matches the platform member's name N, plan_version's VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates contains no entry for that manifest referencing N -- an OptionalDepUpdate is only produced when a matching optionalDependencies entry already exists to update, never speculatively created.

Given a workspace where no Fixed group anywhere has any GroupMember::PlatformManifest members (only Package members across every group), plan_version's VersionPlan.platform_writes and VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates are both empty Vecs -- no regression for workspaces without platform packages. (VersionPlan carries no per-group partition, so this is necessarily a workspace-wide assertion, not a per-group one.)

Given a Fixed group whose owner package receives no version bump this run (outcome.severities for the owner is Severity::None, so no PlannedBump is produced for it), plan_version produces no PlatformWrite and no OptionalDepUpdate entry for that group's GroupMember::PlatformManifest members, even if those platform manifests exist on disk -- platform-manifest writes are strictly driven by an actual owner PlannedBump, never speculative.

Given a Fixed group whose owner has two GroupMember::PlatformManifest siblings (e.g. linux-x64-gnu and darwin-arm64 targets) and receives a real bump to Y, plan_version's platform_writes contains one PlatformWrite entry per platform member (two entries total), each with its own manifest path and matching from/version values -- multiple platform manifests under one owner are all covered, not just the first.

Given the AC-007 scenario (owner with two GroupMember::PlatformManifest siblings, both bumped) where the owner's canonical manifest has matching optionalDependencies entries for both platform names, plan_version's VersionPlan.optional_dep_updates contains exactly one OptionalDepUpdate entry for the owner's canonical manifest path, whose `updates` field contains both (name, version) pairs -- entries are merged per target manifest path, never duplicated as separate OptionalDepUpdate entries pointing at the same path.

Given a Fixed group's platform manifest file declared in group config does not exist on disk, or exists but cannot be parsed as valid content for its ecosystem (malformed JSON/TOML), and the owner package receives a real bump this run, plan_version returns Err(GraphError) surfacing the underlying manifest read failure -- it does not silently omit the PlatformWrite entry, does not panic, and does not produce a partial VersionPlan.

Fix 1 (apply.rs active_ecosystems): given a VersionPlan whose plan.bumps is empty but plan.platform_writes contains one entry pointing at an npm-ecosystem manifest path (e.g. 'platform/my-lib.linux-x64-gnu/package.json'), ApplyOptions.refresh_lockfiles == true, and opts.transient == false, calling apply_version_plan causes the npm lockfile (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, or bun.lockb -- whichever exists on disk at the workspace root) to be included in ApplyOutcome.staged. apply_version_plan's lockfile_ecosystems staging table (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:411-421) is not filtered by npm workspace kind, so any of the four npm lockfile filenames present on disk is staged, not specifically the one matching the detected workspace kind. Note: apply_version_plan has no npm lockfile REFRESH subprocess at all (only Cargo via `cargo update` and Pypi via `uv lock`/`poetry lock` at apply.rs:353-407) -- this is true for every plan, before and after this fix, npm-touching or not. This criterion asserts staging only; ApplyOutcome.lockfile_refresh_results contains no npm entry, matching the pre-existing, unchanged behavior for an ordinary plan.bumps-only plan touching an npm manifest.

Fix 1 (apply.rs active_ecosystems): given the AC-009 scenario but using plan.optional_dep_updates instead of plan.platform_writes (plan.bumps empty, one OptionalDepUpdate entry pointing at an npm-ecosystem manifest path, refresh_lockfiles == true, transient == false), calling apply_version_plan causes the same npm-lockfile staging-only behavior described in AC-009 -- the npm lockfile present on disk is included in ApplyOutcome.staged, and no npm entry appears in ApplyOutcome.lockfile_refresh_results.

Fix 1 regression: given an ordinary VersionPlan with only plan.bumps entries populated (plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates both empty, as in every plan before this track), calling apply_version_plan with refresh_lockfiles == true produces byte-for-byte the same ApplyOutcome.lockfile_refresh_results and the same ApplyOutcome.staged as before this track's change -- confirmed by all pre-existing apply.rs tests passing unmodified. (active_ecosystems itself is a function-local binding with no external visibility; this criterion is expressed against ApplyOutcome's public fields, which are what a test can actually observe.)

Fix 2 (apply.rs platform_writes precondition): given a VersionPlan.platform_writes entry whose `from` field does not match the actual on-disk current_version() of that platform manifest at apply time (drift -- e.g. someone hand-edited the platform package.json between plan and apply), calling apply_version_plan returns Err(GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion { path, expected_from, expected_to, found }) where path is the platform manifest's path, expected_from is PlatformWrite.from, expected_to is PlatformWrite.version, and found is the actual on-disk version -- the platform manifest is not written. This criterion applies only when the on-disk current_version() equals neither PlatformWrite.from nor PlatformWrite.version -- see AC-012b for the current==version idempotent-retry case, which is not an error.

Fix 2 idempotent-retry case: given a VersionPlan.platform_writes entry whose `from` field does NOT match the platform manifest's on-disk current_version(), but that on-disk current_version() already equals PlatformWrite.version (the platform manifest was already written to its target by a prior, interrupted apply run), calling apply_version_plan treats this as success -- it does not write the manifest again and does not return UnexpectedManifestVersion, but still appends the manifest path to modified_paths so it is re-staged on retry.

Fix 2 regression: given a VersionPlan.platform_writes entry whose `from` field exactly matches the platform manifest's actual on-disk current_version() at apply time (the ordinary, non-drifted case), calling apply_version_plan succeeds and the platform manifest's on-disk version is exactly `version` after apply -- no behavior change from before this fix for the non-drifted path.

reasoning: Verified against live code before drafting: (1) GroupMember::PlatformManifest{owner,role,path,name} confirmed at crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:28-34. (2) PlatformWrite{manifest,version} and OptionalDepUpdate{manifest,updates} confirmed at crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs:45-55, both currently 2-field structs -- PlatformWrite's `from` field is a genuine addition, documented in api_surface. (3) commands/version.rs plan_version hardcodes platform_writes/optional_dep_updates to Vec::new() at lines 262-263 -- confirmed, this is the exact gap the requirement describes. (4) apply.rs's two dispatch loops for platform_writes (lines 244-252) and optional_dep_updates (lines 254-262) exist and are unconditional/no-precondition for platform_writes, confirmed by direct read -- unlike the sibling bump loops at lines 146-161 and 181-214 which do check current==expected and return GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion (confirmed shape at error.rs:157-162) on drift. (5) active_ecosystems derivation at apply.rs:325-349 is confirmed to iterate only plan.bumps -- platform_writes/optional_dep_updates paths are never consulted, confirming Fix 1's dormant-bug claim. (6) pr_body.rs's compose_pr_body (lines 16-27) is confirmed to call plan_version directly with no independent VersionPlan construction in its production path -- so unlike the requirement's grouping of snapshot.rs and pr_body.rs together as 'deferred', pr_body.rs needs zero code change and this is stated as a confirmed fact in non_goals, not an assumption. snapshot.rs's plan_snapshot (lines 131-143) does independently construct a VersionPlan with synthetic snapshot_versions and remains a genuinely separate, deferred producer. (7) The Manifest trait's iter_dependencies() (callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:34) returning DependencyEntry{name,kind,spec,inherited} with DepKind::Optional as a variant (callisto-model/src/dependency.rs:13-19) is the mechanism AC-003/AC-004 rely on to detect an existing optionalDependencies entry without speculatively inventing one. (8) OpenContext/open() exist at the callisto-graph crate level (used by apply.rs and manifest_cache.rs), confirming plan_version has the infrastructure available to open and read a platform manifest's current_version() at plan time for AC-002/AC-008, without needing a new manifest-reading primitive built from scratch. No TBDs remain; genuinely unresolved implementation choices (exact function name for the new plan_version helper, whether platform manifest reads are cached) are left to the planning stage since they don't affect observable behavior. (9) CORRECTION (see revision_note): AC-002b originally claimed a real, disk-discovered Cargo platform manifest could be classified as GroupMember::PlatformManifest and flow through plan_version end-to-end. TASK-3's implementer confirmed via walk.rs:199 (Ecosystem::Npm-only gate on IdentityIndex.platform registration) and via an empirical real-pipeline run that this is false -- no Cargo.toml can currently become a GroupMember::PlatformManifest through real discovery. Chose correction option (a): narrowed AC-002b to test the OpenContext/workspace-inheritance resolution logic directly against a fixture-constructed GroupMember::PlatformManifest, rather than converting it to a non_goal, because the resolution logic itself (AC-002's format-agnostic machinery) is real, already-scoped work this track owns and can prove today -- deferring the whole criterion to a non_goal would have discarded a legitimate, currently-provable guarantee (that the machinery is format-agnostic) along with the genuinely out-of-scope discovery gap. Added a new non_goals entry making the walk.rs Cargo-discovery gap and its deferral explicit, since the prior non_goals item 6 ('this track assumes group config already passed that validation') implicitly and incorrectly assumed Cargo discovery already worked.
revision_note: Corrected AC-002b per TASK-3 lambda-implementer's confirmed contradiction: walk.rs:199 only registers platform-manifest identities for Ecosystem::Npm (no Cargo branch), so no Cargo.toml can be classified as GroupMember::PlatformManifest through the real discovery pipeline today -- verified both by code inspection and by an empirical real-pipeline run where a Cargo.toml platform sibling with `version.workspace = true` resolved as an ordinary GroupMember::Package, leaving plan.platform_writes empty. Applied correction option (a): narrowed AC-002b to verify the OpenContext/workspace-inheritance-resolution logic (AC-002's format-agnostic machinery) directly against a fixture-constructed GroupMember::PlatformManifest member, rather than relying on real discovery to produce one -- this is honestly provable today and does not require the walk.rs discovery extension. Added a new non_goals entry explicitly naming 'extending walk.rs's Ecosystem::Npm gate to Ecosystem::Cargo' as out-of-scope, deferred, future work, and clarifying that this track's machinery is format-agnostic and will work once that discovery extension ships. Sibling criterion AC-007 (npm multi-sibling platform writes) required no change -- it is unaffected and already satisfied by TASK-2's landed code (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:264-302). AC-001 and criteria built on the 'AC-001 scenario' (AC-003 through AC-007b) required no change since AC-001 was always implicitly npm-scoped and npm discovery is unaffected by this gap.
